proposals.impact: lift open rate across lower-performing automations by adapting the subject line pattern from the 66% open rate sequence
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Avoidance sits at 52.63% and Money Worship at 37.5%. The gap between best and worst is nearly 30 percentage points. Subject line pattern, sender name, or preview text in the Vigilance sequence is doing something the other two are not. The Worship sequence in particular — lowest open rate, second-highest send volume — is the biggest drain. Adapting the Vigilance subject line structure into the Worship email-01 subject line is a one-field edit with measurable upside.
proposals.proposal: Pull the subject line from email-01 in the Money Vigilance automation and compare its structure — length, presence of a question, specificity of the fear it names — against the Money Worship email-01 subject line. Rewrite the Worship subject line to match the Vigilance pattern: name a specific, uncomfortable behaviour the reader will recognise in themselves rather than a category or a virtue. The edit lives in one markdown frontmatter field and can be A/B observed across the next sends without touching any other automation logic.

proposals.new_text: subject: "Why do you keep checking your balance — then feel worse for looking?"

proposals.impact: unblock automated content publishing — Daily Blog Post workflow has failed, leaving queue at 1 with no new post shipped today
proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 07:19 on 1 July. The content queue shows one post queued and 47 published. That queued post has not shipped. With the Funnel-Hack Digest also failing and Fred Propose having failed the previous cycle, three of fifteen workflow runs in the window have concluded in failure. The blog is the top-of-funnel content surface for organic traffic and the quiz entry point. A day without a published post is a day without a new indexed page and without a fresh reason for email subscribers to click through.
proposals.proposal: Open the Daily Blog Post workflow file and read the last failed run log. The most common causes for this class of CI failure in Astro content pipelines are: a malformed frontmatter field in the queued post, a missing required schema field added after the post was drafted, or an API rate-limit on the publishing step. Check the queued post's frontmatter against src/content.config.ts schema, fix the offending field, and commit. Do not touch the workflow file itself — that path is blocked. The fix lives in the queued content file.
proposals.new_text: Identify the queued post file in src/content/blog/ (the one with no pubDate or a future pubDate beyond today), open it, and confirm every required frontmatter field matches the schema: title, description, pubDate (ISO 8601), tags (array), and any fields added since the file was drafted. If a field is missing or malformed, add or correct it. Commit the corrected file with message "fix: queued post frontmatter so Daily Blog Post workflow can publish".

proposals.impact: drive first quiz sessions — 0 starts in 48 hours means nobody is finding or clicking into the quiz from the homepage
proposals.observation: The quiz shows zero sessions and zero starts across a 48-hour window. This is not a completion-rate problem — nobody is reaching the quiz at all. The homepage is the most likely entry point for new visitors arriving from blog posts or social. If the homepage call-to-action for the quiz is below the fold, visually quiet, or framed as a generic "take the quiz" prompt rather than naming the specific discomfort it resolves, visitors are skipping it entirely. One sentence change to the CTA above the fold can move sessions from zero to measurable.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the homepage quiz CTA so it names the specific behavioural tension the quiz surfaces — the gap between earning well and having nothing to show for it — rather than describing the quiz as a category ("find your money type" or similar). The copy should speak to the 25-35 earner who suspects the problem is them, not their income. One sentence, above the fold, in the existing CTA component. No layout change. No new component.

proposals.new_text: Answer seven questions and see the specific pattern that's kept your income and your savings moving in opposite directions.
